conclusion.root_cause: Baseline is dominated by host-side launch overhead, not device work: msprof shows the 1024-element kernel runs 1.3 us while the eval walltime floor is 75 us at 1K, 64K and 1M elements alike, so ~63 us per call is spent in the Python/triton dispatch path (logger.debug + kwargs dispatch + lambda grid + torch_device_fn.device guard + JITFunction.run) versus 11.6 us for the reference. The 4096x4096 case (0.60 ms) is scalar/issue-bound, not memory-bound: aiv_scalar 0.627 of a 599 us kernel with mte2 0.118 and mte3 0.127, because a 16384-program grid of 1024-element blocks costs ~150 scalar/flag instructions per program.
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: Baseline round: geo_mean 0.1304 with min_speedup 0.0819 (selu_-timing-11, 4096x4096 fp32). Every workload is slower than the reference; the profile attributes the small/medium floor entirely to host dispatch and the large cases to per-program scalar issue overhead. No prior measurement existed to compare against.
conclusion.next_suggestion: Reduce per-call host dispatch cost first (biggest lever: 4 of 12 timing workloads sit at the 75 us floor and 4 more are only ~14 us of kernel): bypass JITFunction.run with a cached compiled launcher (flag_gems libentry or a direct compiled-kernel handle), replace the lambda grid with a precomputed tuple, and drop the device-guard context and logger.debug from the hot path, keeping BLOCK_SIZE=1024 and the arithmetic identical so the effect is isolated.
conclusion.debug_lesson: Candidate admission rejects any torch.ops.aten fallback even for non-contiguous inputs, so general stride support must live in the candidate kernel (4D padded shape/stride decomposition).
conclusion.strategy_evolution: Established that the forbidden aten fallback in the seed must be replaced by an in-candidate strided kernel (preflight rejected torch.ops.aten.selu_), and that the next optimization must target host dispatch before tiling.

import triton
import triton.language as tl

        return False

        return False

            compiled = compiled.result()
        stream = _driver.active.get_current_stream(device)

            grid0,
            1,
            1,
            stream,
            compiled.function,
            compiled.packed_metadata,
            None,
            None,
            None,

conclusion.root_cause: The intended launch-path bypass never took effect. JITFunction.run sets kwargs['debug'] and calls _flagprism.apply_compile_options(kwargs) before binder(), so the options that feed compute_cache_key differ from the ones obtained by my bare binder(x, n, BLOCK_SIZE=1024) call; the recomputed key therefore missed on every invocation. _fast_launch returned False each time and the caller executed the stock literal kernel[grid](...) launch, so round 2 was functionally identical to round 1 (same 66-69 us host floor, exact numerics).
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: Expected ~30 us lower per-call floor on the 9 launch-bound workloads; observed only 75.0 -> 67.2 us (timing-0), 79.4 -> 65.8 (timing-2), 86.0 -> 66.4 (timing-10) and essentially unchanged 4096x4096 cases (0.604/0.601/0.604 ms), giving geo_mean 0.13037 -> 0.12965, i.e. no gain. The gap is fully explained by the fast path never launching: the in-process probe shows _SLOW remained False, the recomputed key's kernel_cache.get() returned None (compiled_type NoneType), so every call still ran the stock JIT launch at ~69 us/call in batch mode, matching the observed eval floor. Reference latencies also moved between rounds (11.6 -> 8.2-10.4 us on the small workloads), so the small delta is within environment noise rather than a real effect.
conclusion.next_suggestion: Key the cached launch on triton's own `specialization` list returned by binder (which is independent of the injected options) plus BLOCK_SIZE, and capture the compiled handle by diffing kernel_cache keys before/after the stock launch instead of recomputing the option-dependent cache key. Also use x.device.index instead of get_current_device. Re-verify on the target that the fast path actually launches (compiled handle found) and that one call performs exactly one kernel execution.
conclusion.debug_lesson: A cached compiled-kernel fast path must be validated in-process: assert that the lookup actually hits (here kernel_cache.get(key) was None on every call) instead of inferring engagement from the measured latency alone. Recomputing triton's cache key from binder() alone is invalid because run() injects FlagPrism compile options and debug into the options before binding.
conclusion.strategy_evolution: Round 1 showed host dispatch dominates 9 of 12 timing workloads; round 2 attempted a cached compiled-kernel launch but silently fell back to the JIT path due to a cache-key mismatch. Next round must fix the key derivation and prove engagement on the target before evaluating.
